1. Core Clinical Tension: A 21-year-old previously healthy female presents with subacute intracranial hypertension culminating in acute obtundation due to obstructive hydrocephalus from a solid, homogenously enhancing third ventricular mass obstructing the Foramen of Monro. In the absence of constitutional symptoms, pulmonary lesions, or systemic immunodeficiency, this lesion strongly mimicked a primary brain neoplasm or colloid cyst rather than an isolated infectious granuloma.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The admission evaluation concludes after emergency stabilization, non-contrast cranial CT showing a third ventricular mass with obstructive hydrocephalus, unremarkable chest radiograph, and normal baseline hematology and biochemistry, immediately prior to elective contrast-enhanced MRI and craniotomy with surgical excision.
3. Differential Distinctions: Colloid cysts and primary glial tumors typically occur at the Foramen of Monro; however, histological analysis of the resected specimen demonstrated epithelioid cells and Langhans multinucleated giant cells characteristic of a tuberculoma rather than neoplastic glial proliferation or a mucinous epithelial cyst.
case_prompt: A 21-year-old right-handed female was brought to the emergency department after a sudden onset of unconsciousness lasting for 6 hours. Her family reported a 3-month history of persistent headache and intermittent vomiting. On physical examination, her Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score was 13. Funduscopic examination revealed bilateral papilledema. Cranial nerve and motor examinations showed no focal neurological deficits. Initial laboratory evaluation revealed hematology and serum biochemistry parameters within normal limits. Serological tests for HIV and hepatitis were negative. A plain chest radiograph was unremarkable. Emergent non-contrast cranial computed tomography (CT) demonstrated a third ventricular mass with obstructive hydrocephalus.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered primary presumptive diagnosis based on age and an intraventricular lesion obstructing the Foramen of Monro; ruled out when total surgical excision and histopathology revealed necrotizing granulomatous inflammation rather than neoplastic glial proliferation.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: On clinical and radiological grounds, the diagnosis was made as neoplasm that could be a glial tumor, lymphoma or colloid cyst.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the characteristic anatomical location obstructing the Foramen of Monro; excluded intraoperatively and pathologically by a firm, solid, moderately vascular mass with Langhans giant cells rather than a mucinous fluid collection with simple epithelial lining.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: On clinical and radiological grounds, the diagnosis was made as neoplasm that could be a glial tumor, lymphoma or colloid cyst.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered due to homogenous contrast enhancement and T2 hypointensity; excluded by negative HIV serology and absence of malignant lymphoid infiltrates on tissue histopathology.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: On clinical and radiological grounds, the diagnosis was made as neoplasm that could be a glial tumor, lymphoma or colloid cyst.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The diagnostic turning point occurred unexpectedly after right frontal craniotomy and transcallosal transventricular total excision of the third ventricular mass, when histopathological examination revealed epithelioid and Langhans giant cells confirming tuberculoma, leading to full recovery on antituberculous therapy.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Surprisingly, histological examination revealed granulomatous lesion with epitheloid and Langhans cells, consistent with tuberculoma

editor_comments: Distilled strictly to emergency admission presentation. Obstructive third ventricular mass initially presumed to be glioma/colloid cyst; histological discovery of Langhans giant cells established the diagnosis.
